entries.why: Enumerate IAM roles — assumption targets and the identity backbone for service permissions. ListRoles is the account's complete inventory of roles (the walk is checked, and its count compared with GetAccountSummary), and each role is read again because ListRoles omits its permissions boundary and last-used time by AWS's own contract.
entries.persist_configuration_why: On: carries the posture and relationship detail the typed fields do not; no credential location is declared in sensitivity.

containment.why: An IAM role exists in exactly one account and is never shared; the account's ListRoles, read to its end, is the complete list of them. A role it stops naming is a question for the role's falsifier (GetRole), not a deletion.

sensitivity.basis: Read botocore iam ListRoles and GetRole output shapes (Role), ListAttachedRolePolicies, and custom_fn iam_roles_described, 2026-09-28.

locations.reason: Trust policy naming the principals, including third-party accounts, allowed to assume the role; its sts:ExternalId conditions carry the value a third party presents.

entries.why: Enumerate CloudFront distributions — CDN/edge entry points and their origins. Each origin's Origin Access Control (OAC) is resolved and embedded in configuration.
entries.persist_configuration_why: Off: ListDistributions returns Origins.Items[].CustomHeaders.Items[].HeaderValue verbatim, and custom origin headers are commonly a shared secret between CloudFront and the origin. Each origin's access mode (OAC, OAI or none) is kept as the typed field origin_access. Whether each origin is sent any custom header is kept as the typed field origin_custom_headers_present, a boolean per origin: presence only, never the header value or name.

sensitivity.basis: Read botocore cloudfront ListDistributions (DistributionSummary) and GetOriginAccessControl output shapes and custom_fn cloudfront_distributions_with_oac, 2026-09-23.

locations.reason: Custom origin headers are the usual way to hold a shared secret the origin checks (for example an origin-verify header). Only their presence per origin is recorded, as the typed field origin_custom_headers_present; the value is never stored, and neither is the name, which can say which secret it is.
Operator-authored comment.
Each OAC's OriginAccessControlConfig.Description is operator-authored text.
